NOVEL-AND-FEASIBLE IDEATION

STEP 1 — INVENT THE OBSERVABLE:
Standard practice tracks volumetric wear rate (mm³/million cycles) as the primary indicator of liner performance. My observable is the oxidation-induced free radical concentration in the UHMWPE matrix, inferred from electron paramagnetic resonance (EPR) spectroscopy of retrieved liner samples, which directly measures the chemical degradation driving embrittlement rather than just the mechanical wear outcome.

STEP 2 — MAKE THE IMPLEMENTATION BORING:
This observable can be computed from standard mechanical testing equipment already used in orthopedic labs by adding a simple EPR attachment to the existing tensile testing machine, using the same sample preparation methods currently employed for mechanical testing.

NOVELTY STATEMENT:
Standard practice tracks volumetric wear as a mechanical outcome, while my observable measures the chemical degradation (free radical concentration) that precedes and enables the embrittlement failure. The connection is that free radicals disrupt the polymer chain integrity, reducing fatigue-crack-propagation resistance and ultimately leading to increased wear and osteolysis.

PHYSICS CHECK:
The governing physical relation is that free radical concentration (N) follows first-order kinetics: N = N₀e^(-kt), where k is the oxidation rate constant. For a conventional liner, N₀ ≈ 10¹⁶ spins/g and k ≈ 10⁻⁷ s⁻¹. A 20% reduction in fatigue-crack-propagation resistance corresponds to approximately 5×10¹⁵ spins/g, which is physically consistent with polymer degradation literature.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL:
Components: 1) Existing hip simulator for wear testing, 2) Standard tensile testing machine with EPR attachment, 3) Sample preparation kit (microtome, cutting guides), 4) EPR spectrometer (can be added to existing lab equipment), 5) Data acquisition software compatible with existing systems.
Materials: Standard UHMWPE test samples, liquid nitrogen for sample preservation.
Instruments: Hip simulator, tensile tester with EPR capability, microtome.
Procedure: 1) Run hip simulation per ISO 14242, 2) Extract samples at specified intervals, 3) Prepare samples for EPR analysis, 4) Measure free radical concentration, 5) Compare to baseline and threshold.
All components are commercially available; no new sensor development required.

BURDEN LEDGER (STANDARD-PRACTICE PARITY):
- Installability: Same as standard practice - no new installation requirements
- Operability: Minimal additional training for EPR operation (1-2 days)
- Maintenance: Same maintenance schedule as existing equipment
- Cost class: Moderate increase (~$50k for EPR attachment) but provides additional degradation insight
The approach maintains same deployment burden while providing earlier warning of failure through chemical degradation detection rather than just mechanical wear measurement.

EXECUTABLE TEST:
Protocol: Run 5 million cycles on hip simulator with test liner, then perform EPR analysis on 3 samples from different liner locations. Repeat every 2 million cycles until 10 million cycles completed.
Instruments: Hip simulator, EPR spectrometer, sample preparation tools.
Pass threshold: Free radical concentration below 5×10¹⁵ spins/g at all time points
Fail threshold: Free radical concentration exceeds 5×10¹⁵ spins/g at any time point
Duration: 10 million cycles (approximately 3-4 weeks of continuous testing)
Kill criterion: Immediate test failure if free radical concentration exceeds 5×10¹⁵ spins/g at any sampling point
